newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway upgrades oil, gas reserves by 16 pct.
newsitem.headline: Norway upgrades oil, gas reserves by 16 pct.

text.p: Oil-rich Norway said on Wednesday it had upgraded estimates of recoverable hydrocarbon reserves on the Norwegian continental shelf (NCS) by nearly 16 percent to 12.5 billion cubic metres of oil equivalent, or 78.6 billion barrels.
In 1995 the country's Oil Directorate (OD) projected recoverable reserves at around 10.8 billion cubic metres of oil equivalent.

In its latest report, the OD said the NCS was estimated to hold 6.5 billion cubic metres of oil and six billion cubic metres of gas. The range of uncertainty in the total estimate was between 9.5 to 16.5 billion cubic metres, it said.
Total discovered reserves amounted to between 7.5 to 10.5 billion cubic metres, while undiscovered hydrocarbons were put at between two and six billion cubic metres.
The OD said the increase was chiefly due to an upward adjustment in the recovery factor for in place reserves.

"Based on an anticipation that 50 percent of the in place oil resources and 75 percent of the in place gas resources will be recovered, resources from possible measure for increased recovery are estimated to be 790 million cubic metres of oil and 420 billion cubic metres of gas," the OD's report said.

It said the total increase in estimates of recoverable hydrocarbon resources of 1.015 billion cubic metres of oil equivalent corresponded to 83 percent of total Norwegian oil and gas production between 1971 and 1997.
According to the OD figures Norway pumped 1.49 billion cubic metres of oil, 492 billion cubic metres of gas and 48 million tonnes of natural gas liquids up to December 31, 1996.

Norway's daily output currently ranges between 3.0 and 3.2 million barrels. The Scandinavian country, which consumes just 150,000 barrels per day (bpd), is western Europe's largest oil producer and the world's second biggest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia.
The OD said crude output was expected to reach a peak at 3.7 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2000.
"The uncertainty in this forecast varies from 3.2 to 4.4 million bpd," it said.
